sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Destination-Based Taxation**: Tax is collected at the point of consumption rather than the point of origin, benefiting consuming states.
• **Value-Added Tax Chain**: Input Tax Credit (ITC) mechanism ensures seamless credit flow across the supply chain, eliminating cascading tax effects (tax-on-tax).
• **Constitutional Amendment**: Introduced via the **Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016**, inserting Articles 246A, 269A, and 279A.
• **GST Council Composition**: Chaired by the Union Finance Minister, with the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue/Finance and all State Finance/Taxation Ministers as members.
• **Voting Mechanism**: Decisions require a majority of not less than **three-fourths (75%)** of the weighted votes cast; the Centre has 1/3rd weightage and all states combined have 2/3rd weightage.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Consumption-Heavy States**: States like Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Gujarat generate the highest GST revenues due to large industrial and service footprints.
• **Destination State Implications**: Consuming states (e.g., Bihar, Uttar Pradesh) benefit increasingly over time due to the destination-based nature of IGST apportionment.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Multiple tax slabs causing classification disputes, delayed refunds, compliance burden on MSMEs, and structural revenue shortfall concerns for states.
• **Policy Interventions**: Rationalization of tax rates, integration with e-invoicing, expansion of analytics via AI/ML on GSTN, and continuous broadening of the tax base.

items.title: Mnemonic for GST Council Voting Weights
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **"C1 S2 = 3/4"** (Centre 1 part, States 2 parts, total 3 parts; requiring 3/4th majority).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Centre holds 1/3rd voting weight, States hold 2/3rd voting weight; any resolution needs 75% affirmative votes.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly verifies factual statements regarding federal veto power and voting thresholds in the GST Council.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: **Article 279A** = Council; **Article 246A** = Concurrent Power to tax GST; **Article 269A** = IGST & Inter-state commerce.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently misleads candidates by stating that the Union Finance Minister has a veto power in the GST Council. In reality, all decisions require a 3/4th majority, meaning neither the Centre nor the States alone can veto or pass a decision without cross-voting/consensus.

Mains Value Addition: Frame the GST Council as a unique institutional experiment in 'Cooperative Federalism' enshrined in the Constitution, while noting friction points over cess distribution and compensation as instances of 'Coercive' or 'Frictional' federalism.

keyTakeaways: GST replaced a fragmented indirect tax regime with a unified, destination-based tax system governed constitutionally by Article 279A.
The GST Council operates on a unique weighted voting formula (Centre 1/3rd, States 2/3rd, 75% threshold) embodying cooperative federalism.
Critical mechanisms like Input Tax Credit (ITC), IGST apportionment, and e-invoicing drive compliance while eliminating cascading tax effects.
